text.name: eq_help_temperament_2
text.text: You lose your multiplier if you speed up into a canter or gallop, collide with an obstacle or miss the next manoeuvre. Feeding your horses treats like carrots is also a great way to improve Temperament.

text.name: eq_help_temperament_1
text.text: Temperament training is all about teaching your horse control. Start a routine by moving into a walk and holding that pace for a short interval. The training program will then ask you for a new manoeuvre to hold. Achieve it within a few seconds to keep the combo going.

text.name: eq_help_agility_2
text.text: You lose your multiplier if you don't clear a new obstacle in time, or if you come to a complete halt or drop back to a walk. Jumping without an obstacle gives some training benefit but doesn't raise your multiplier.

text.name: eq_help_agility_1
text.text: Agility is all about clearing jumps, though you can gain a little from cycling through the gaits. Clear obstacles successfully to build an Agility training multiplier.

text.name: eq_train_combo_none
text.text: Clear a jump to start a combo

text.name: eq_help_speed_2
text.text: Walk or rest to recover before the next sprint. Below 30% a horse recovers quickly, a fit one even more so. Walking recovers just as fast, but it uses up the riding bar. Feeding your horses high-energy corn is a great way to improve speed training.

text.name: eq_help_speed_1
text.text: Speed training improves with sprints. Gallop while the horse is fresh, with exertion under 25%. Gains fade as it tires and stop entirely at 55%.

text.name: eq_help_stamina_2
text.text: Above 85% the horse is blowing hard and learns more slowly: trot to ease off and keep the gains going, and try to hold a long canter. Stamina also increases how long your horse can train each day.

text.name: eq_help_stamina_1
text.text: Stamina comes from runs at a canter or gallop. Gains build as you hold a steady pace, and are best while you keep exertion in the zone, between 65 and 85%. Galloping tires your horse quickly and reduces your gains without rest.

text.name: eq_help_freestyle_2
text.text: Press Y to switch to a focused stat view. Stats progress the same in any view, but those views give you more information and help. Press H to see these help messages again.

text.name: eq_help_freestyle_1
text.text: Riding trains your horse's stats, and each stat is best trained in a different way. Stamina and Speed learn most from focused work, measured by the Exertion meter: fast bursts for Speed, longer rides for Stamina. Agility and Temperament improve with the combo system: clear jumps in a row to raise Agility, or perform slow manoeuvres to raise Temperament. The riding bar is the horse's energy for the day: once it is full, that horse cannot make any more progress until the next day.

text.name: eq_train_worn
text.text: Riding bar full: this horse cannot train any more today

text.name: eq_train_sprint_warm
text.text: Warmed up: keep galloping for Sprint

text.name: eq_train_sprint_rest
text.text: Rest below 10% to warm up again

text.name: eq_help_speed_3
text.text: Two good sprints warm your horse up. Keep galloping and press W when Sprint! shows: your horse runs 25% faster, ignores exertion and trains speed three times as fast. Keep tapping W to spur it on and the Sprint lasts longer, though each tap counts for less as it goes on. Drop out of a gallop and it ends. Then rest below 10% exertion before warming up again.

text.name: eq_help_stamina_3
text.text: Keep up a high tempo: every 20 seconds of unbroken canter or gallop raises your tempo, up to x5, and stamina gains grow up to 2.5 times. From x3 a gallop builds tempo twice as fast. Blowing hard stops the climb and for more than 5 seconds ends the streak; so does more than a couple of seconds below a canter. A quick trot drops exertion fast if you need it.

text.name: eq_train_tempo_none
text.text: Canter or gallop to build tempo
